incidents.symptom: An opening can contain correct storyboard beats yet still fail to establish what kind of world/place the player is seeing.
incidents.generalized_failure: Reviewers with design context infer missing setting information instead of measuring cold-start visual comprehension.
incidents.invariant: A cold observer must be able to describe the setting, ordinary activity, important relationships and the disruptive change without creator rationale.

incidents.symptom: A technically valid default idle loop can feel uncanny, creepy or stylistically wrong for the target audience.
incidents.generalized_failure: Asset-bundled animation silently determines character personality and critics inspect silhouettes/stills instead of motion.
incidents.invariant: Controlled characters require an explicit motion profile and motion-quality claims require observation over time.
mechanisms: explicit player idle/move aliases and speeds

incidents.symptom: A catastrophic story event can reduce to actors translating/disappearing while captions claim thunder, rupture or danger.
incidents.generalized_failure: Narrative importance is not compiled into coordinated visual/audio/environmental event direction.
incidents.invariant: Major events must declare and render enough coordinated cause/reaction/environment/effect channels for perceived magnitude to match narrative magnitude.

incidents.symptom: A story expects the player to know who caused an event even though the experience does not make the causal source perceptible.
incidents.generalized_failure: Critics import antagonist causality from the storyboard instead of checking what a cold player infers.
incidents.invariant: Known intended causes must visibly precede/connect to their effects unless ambiguity is deliberately specified.

incidents.symptom: A major abstract story capability is represented by an arbitrary primitive that has no readable meaning.
incidents.generalized_failure: Internal semantic IDs are mistaken for player comprehension.
incidents.invariant: Major semantic objects need at least two intentional readability channels and a cold observer should infer their role from presentation/behavior.

incidents.symptom: A protagonist can walk through visible solid props because rendered geometry and navigation blocking are authored separately.
incidents.generalized_failure: Physicality is optional controller metadata rather than a property of world entities/archetypes.
incidents.invariant: Visible solid world archetypes own their collider intent and interactive traversal must verify that world geometry behaves physically.

incidents.symptom: Opening, tutorial and mission prompts can overlap, or tutorial text can name an action without identifying the actual target/control.
incidents.generalized_failure: Experience modes and tutorial goals are presentation conventions instead of explicit runtime/spec contracts.
incidents.invariant: Exactly one experience mode owns the player goal; each tutorial step binds one skill, target/control, action, success detector and feedback.
